tasks.title: FloorMapDrawable: dispose cached images and move image loading off the Draw path
acceptance: Closes MASTER-025 (UIKIT-002) ONLY. MASTER-013 (UIKIT-001) moved to Session 6 at Gate 2. The public surface is exactly the one frozen in C:\Users\dmarq\Development\Repos\dungeon-master\.dir-sdlc\sessions\2026-08-24-async-disposal-and-threading-discipline\contracts\floor-map-drawable.md as amended: the class declaration stays `public sealed class FloorMapDrawable : IDrawable` with NO IDisposable and NO Dispose(); `public void ClearObjectImageCache()` keeps its signature and gains per-entry disposal; and `public async Task PreloadObjectImagesAsync()` is added with exactly that signature. No other member is added, removed or renamed. Deviating from the frozen surface is a contract-change escalation, not a judgment call: T3 consumes it.

The undisposed-image leak MASTER-013 describes is KNOWINGLY LEFT IN PLACE and is Session 6's work. Do not add IDisposable, do not add Dispose(), and do not let the finished file read as though the leak were addressed. One half of it does land here and only for this reason: your preload amplifies it. Today _imageCache populates lazily, holding only the kinds actually drawn; after your change PreloadObjectImagesAsync populates an entry for every ObjectKind the active pack declares in ObjectAssetCatalogue.Paths, and ObjectKind has 37 members - verified by `grep -cE "^\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z]*\s*(=|,)" src/DungeonMaster.Domain/Entities/Floor/ObjectKind.cs` returning 37. So without disposal the images abandoned per ClearObjectImageCache() call would rise from 'the kinds the user drew' to 'up to the whole pack', on every pack change. Disposing inside ClearObjectImageCache() holds the leak at or below where it is today and needs no file you do not own. Say all of this in your report so the reviewer does not read MASTER-013 as closed.

`private Microsoft.Maui.Graphics.IImage? LoadOrGetImage(ObjectKind kind)` is a pure cache read: it performs a dictionary lookup and returns the value or null. It contains no call to FileSystem, no call to PlatformImage, and starts no task.

Running `grep -n "GetAwaiter()\.GetResult()\|\.Wait()" src/DungeonMaster.App/Graphics/FloorMapDrawable.cs` from C:\Users\dmarq\Development\Repos\dungeon-master\.claude-worktrees\dir\2026-08-24-async-disposal-and-threading-discipline returns no line. It returns two lines today (291, a comment; 304, the blocking load), so both the comment and the call must go. Paste the command and its output.

PreloadObjectImagesAsync writes to _imageCache only on the thread that called it. There is no Task.Run, no Thread, no Parallel call, and no other write to _imageCache anywhere in the file off the calling thread. State how you confirmed this by reading the finished file.

Both Dispose() and PreloadObjectImagesAsync() catch per entry so one failing image does not abort the rest, and each catch site carries a comment stating why the failure is ignorable at that point - a failed native release must not block the remaining handles; a failed decode renders as the existing missing-object placeholder. A bare `catch { }` with no comment fails this criterion (backend discipline: never swallow an error to keep a path quiet).

Both the per-entry disposal in ClearObjectImageCache() and PreloadObjectImagesAsync() catch per entry so one failure does not abort the rest, and each catch site carries a comment stating why the failure is ignorable at that point - a failed native release must not block the remaining handles; a failed decode renders as the existing missing-object placeholder. A bare `catch { }` with no comment fails this criterion (backend discipline: never swallow an error to keep a path quiet).

tasks.title: HandCursorBehavior: cache the per-pointer-event cursor reflection
acceptance: Closes MASTER-039 (UIKIT-020) ONLY, and touches exactly one file: src/DungeonMaster.App/Behaviors/HandCursorBehavior.cs. MASTER-006 (UIKIT-003, the undetached pan recogniser) and MASTER-062 (UIKIT-017, the unsynchronised long-press flags) moved to Session 6 at Gate 2, so src/DungeonMaster.App/Behaviors/CanvasLongPressDetector.cs and src/DungeonMaster.App/Behaviors/HoverOrLongPressBehavior.cs are owned by NO task in this session and MUST NOT be edited. If you believe one of them needs a change to complete your work, stop and escalate.

HandCursorBehavior.SetCursor no longer calls typeof(Microsoft.UI.Xaml.UIElement).GetProperty("ProtectedCursor", ...) or Microsoft.UI.Input.InputSystemCursor.Create(shape) per invocation. The PropertyInfo is hoisted into a static readonly field and one InputSystemCursor is cached per BehaviorCursorShape. SetCursor runs on every PointerEntered and every PointerExited on every view carrying the behavior, which is what makes the repeated work worth removing.

The null-lookup path is no longer silently repeated forever. The audit notes that if the ProtectedCursor lookup returns null the code does nothing and repeats the lookup on every subsequent pointer event; hoisting it into a static readonly field resolves that by construction. State in your report which behaviour you chose when the cached PropertyInfo is null, and make sure the choice is visible in the code rather than implicit.

Do NOT claim a performance improvement you did not measure. Audit entry UIKIT-020 says plainly "I did not measure the cost and do not claim it is perceptible", and neither may you. The justification is removing unnecessary repeated work on a high-frequency input path, not a measured speedup. A report asserting a measured gain fails this criterion.

The PUBLIC surface of HandCursorBehavior is unchanged: no constructor signature, no public property (including the Shape bindable property), no public method and no public event is added, removed or altered. tasks.title: Infrastructure: make the ConfigureAwait decision deliberate
acceptance: Closes MASTER-153 (INFRA-015), severity S5. The decision to apply ConfigureAwait(false) was taken by the USER at Gate 2, not by the architect, on the evidence recorded in C:\Users\dmarq\Development\Repos\dungeon-master\.dir-sdlc\sessions\2026-08-24-async-disposal-and-threading-discipline\contracts\infrastructure-configureawait.md: CA2007 is intended for libraries and its documented suppression case is UI application code such as WinForms/WPF event handlers, which is DungeonMaster.App and not DungeonMaster.Infrastructure. Read that contract before starting; do not re-open the decision.

Every await expression in the four owned Infrastructure files carries .ConfigureAwait(false). There are 9 awaits across 4 files, verified by `grep -rn "await " --include=*.cs src/DungeonMaster.Infrastructure --exclude-dir=obj --exclude-dir=Migrations | wc -l` returning 9: DependencyInjection.cs:56,58; DungeonReadRepository.cs:19,21,39,41; DungeonWriteRepository.cs:17,48; UnitOfWorkFactory.cs:16. Audit entry INFRA-015 names only the two repository files; the other three awaits are in scope on the same reasoning and this discrepancy must be reported.

Three of the nine are `await using var dbContext = await dbContextFactory.CreateDbContextAsync(ct);` declarations (DependencyInjection.cs:56, DungeonReadRepository.cs:19, DungeonReadRepository.cs:39), which carry two awaits each. Establish the correct syntax by COMPILING it, not by predicting it, and do not state a compiler error code you have not observed. If the disposal await cannot carry ConfigureAwait(false) without a shape you judge harms readability, apply it to the inner factory await only, name the exact line, and say so in your report.

Nothing else changes: no signature, no lifetime, no behaviour, no entity property type. src/DungeonMaster.App is untouched, so the view models' final continuations still resume on the UI thread - which is the audit's stated intent. docs/persistence-contract.md governs entity property types; you introduce no change it covers.

A source-scanning guard test lives in C:\Users\dmarq\Development\Repos\dungeon-master\.claude-worktrees\dir\2026-08-24-async-disposal-and-threading-discipline\src\DungeonMaster.Tests\Infrastructure\Async\ asserting that every non-comment line containing `await ` in the four scoped files also contains `.ConfigureAwait(false)`.
